newsitem.title: USA: CBOT's Arbor objects to CFTC wheat comment period.
newsitem.headline: CBOT's Arbor objects to CFTC wheat comment period.

text.p: Chicago Board of Trade Chairman Pat Arbor on Thursday said he objected to a public comment period on changes needed to the CBOT wheat contract when no changes had yet been approved by the CBOT Board of Directors.

Arbor told Reuters in an interview that he wrote to Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Chairwoman Brooksley Born, saying he did not understand why she would consider opening a comment period now.
"I don't know what you're going to put out for comment because we don't have anything," Arbor said. "Any attempt to put something out for comment will just invite a multitude of opinions."

CFTC's Born said on Monday that she would decide within two weeks whether to seek public comment on the exchange's wheat contract. CFTC recently extended a comment period on controversial changes to the CBOT corn and delivery specifications after it received hundreds of letters.
The CBOT Board of Directors on April 16 voted not to recommend a plan to expand wheat delivery capacity in Toledo.
The CFTC had given the exchange 120 days to come up with a proposal to change the wheat delivery system.
"I am certainly concerned that the CBOT has not been able to come up with a proposal," Born said on Monday. "They haven't given us any sense of where they are going or how long it will take."
Arbor said the proposal was turned down because it did not adequately address problems with the existing contract.
"The problem really wasn't delivery space," Arbor said. "It was the contract design."
Arbor said CBOT claims the majority of U.S. wheat futures trading volume yet the contract is based on soft red winter wheat, which comprised only about 18 percent of last year's U.S. wheat crop.
Futures on hard red winter wheat, the largest wheat variety in the U.S., are traded at the Kansas City Board of Trade.

Arbor said the board should have another proposal on the table by mid-July. The new plan could include a rejig of the current contract or perhaps a proposal for an international wheat contract, he said.
